title: PSG4-RETRY9Q4: a shorter profile from the proved success probability and sharper joint bounds

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, put n=ceil(log2 N). The ONE PSG4-RETRY9Q4 algorithm and exact inherited parameter rule in proof.md recover the entire s from independent ideal source copies with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8>2/3. On EVERY branch including failed attempts, rejected copies, retries, incorrect numerical-label branches and both cutoff aborts, its total charged sequential work T is O(2^((73031/100000)sqrt(n log2 n))). This is its full uniform bit-length envelope for n>=2 with the explicit finite branch covering smaller n. The exact envelope growth index is 1/2. All outside constants are absolute and independent of N,s and outcomes. This holds jointly with the other three resource bounds and clean-only tolerance declaration for the same configuration. The actual profile uses delta(v)=min{d>=0:4*2^d>=9*(2v+1)}, justified by the proved success bound 463/1024>4/9; all derived profile parameters, source precision and literal caps are recomputed for this one configuration. The sharper feasible analysis trial is ceil((7303/10000)sqrt(n log2 n)), with the exact strict capacity certificate in proof.md.

For the same PSG4-RETRY9Q4 algorithm and complete parameter rule in proof.md, the proved malformed-sample fractional guarantee is epsilon(n)=0: all Q acquired source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N>=2 and every s, unconditional full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1-2^-8>2/3 jointly with all four every-branch resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted, and this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
